From 31148a7be723aa9f2e8fbd62424825ab8d577973 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Anas Iqbal <mohd.abd.6602@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 10:51:37 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] Bluetooth: hci_ll: Fix firmware leak on error path

Smatch reports:

drivers/bluetooth/hci_ll.c:587 download_firmware() warn:
'fw' from request_firmware() not released on lines: 544.

In download_firmware(), if request_firmware() succeeds but the returned
firmware content is invalid (no data or zero size), the function returns
without releasing the firmware, resulting in a resource leak.

Fix this by calling release_firmware() before returning when
request_firmware() succeeded but the firmware content is invalid.

Fixes: 371805522f87 ("bluetooth: hci_uart: add LL protocol serdev driver support")
Reviewed-by: Paul Menzel <pmenzel@molgen.mpg.de>
Signed-off-by: Anas Iqbal <mohd.abd.6602@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/bluetooth/hci_ll.c b/drivers/bluetooth/hci_ll.c
index 91acf24f1ef5..91c96ad12342 100644
--- a/drivers/bluetooth/hci_ll.c
+++ b/drivers/bluetooth/hci_ll.c
@@ -541,6 +541,8 @@ static int download_firmware(struct ll_device *lldev)
 	if (err || !fw->data || !fw->size) {
 		bt_dev_err(lldev->hu.hdev, "request_firmware failed(errno %d) for %s",
 			   err, bts_scr_name);
+		if (!err)
+			release_firmware(fw);
 		return -EINVAL;
 	}
 	ptr = (void *)fw->data;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies the error handling logic in the `download_firmware()` function of `drivers/bluetooth/hci_ll.c`. Specifically, in the condition where `request_firmware()` succeeds (`err == 0`) but the returned firmware content is invalid (no data or zero size), a call to `release_firmware(fw)` is added before returning `-EINVAL`. This ensures that the firmware resource is properly freed, preventing a memory leak on that error path. The relationships are limited to a single file and a single logical fix: the added `release_firmware()` call is placed inside the existing error check, conditional on `err == 0`, to cover the case where `request_firmware()` itself did not fail but the firmware data is unusable.
